I also wanted to just briefly call attention to some very exciting work around critical thinking as part of our Portrait of the Graduate at Irvington Middle School, math, special education, and science teachers engage in a book study of Peter Lillodow's Building Thinking Classrooms. The research-based approach aims to revolutionize math learning by inspiring students to take risks and think critically. Tasks are thoughtfully designed to offer students accessible entry points while presenting a challenge slightly exceeding each individual's capabilities. This design encourages students to develop as courageous learners and effective communicators of mathematics. Strategies include visible random grouping, vertical, meaning you stand up, non-permanent surfaces for showing their thinking, and the fact that it's non-permanent promoted risk-taking, and the fact that they're vertical prevents students from disengaging. and it also, Building Thinking Classroom, allows a lot of opportunities for formative assessment. So it's research-based and highly engaging for the students. When students are told to hit the boards, that is their invitation to dive into the task with their group members, try out creative and innovative approaches to determine which method works best. One teacher remarked, it has been a joy to watch. There is an energy in the classroom that is contagious. So we look forward to learning more about building thinking classrooms and highlighting that work for the Board of Education. I've seen it myself and I thought it was quite compelling.
